title: Mormon returns to the Nephites
summary: Mormon goes among the Nephites, repents of his oath not to assist them, and accepts command of their armies again. He has no hope for them because they do not repent or call upon their Creator.

explicit_facts.text: Mormon went among the Nephites and repented of his oath not to assist them.
The Nephites gave Mormon command of their armies again, believing he could deliver them from their afflictions.
Mormon was without hope because the Nephites did not repent and struggled for their lives without calling upon their Creator.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mormon is shown among the Nephites as their army commander.
unspecified_visual_details: Mormon's and the Nephites' appearance, clothing, and the precise setting.

narration.text: I did go forth among the Nephites
I was without hope

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a battle or specific act of repentance beyond what is stated.

title: The city of Jordan holds
summary: The Lamanites come against the Nephites at the city of Jordan and are driven back. They attack again, but the Nephites maintain the city; other Nephite-held cities also block the Lamanites from entering the country ahead.

explicit_facts.text: The Lamanites attacked the Nephites after they had fled to the city of Jordan, but were driven back and did not take it at that time.
The Lamanites came against them again, and the Nephites maintained the city.
Other cities held by Nephites blocked the Lamanites from entering the country before them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephite defenders hold the city against a Lamanite attack.
unspecified_visual_details: The layout and appearance of the city and other strongholds; the number and appearance of combatants.

narration.text: they were driven back
we did maintain the city

prohibited_inventions: Do not show the separate attacks as simultaneous.

title: Lands left ungathered are destroyed
summary: The Lamanites destroy lands whose inhabitants had not been gathered in, burning their towns, villages, and cities. The account notes that 379 years passed.

explicit_facts.text: The Lamanites destroyed lands and settlements whose inhabitants had not been gathered in, burning towns, villages, and cities.
Three hundred and seventy-nine years passed.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A settlement is shown burning as an example of the destruction described.
unspecified_visual_details: Which settlement is shown, the people present, and the visual representation of the passage of time.

narration.text: their towns, and villages, and cities were burned with fire

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The 379 years are a narrated time passage, not a single event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify a particular town or depict an unmentioned named person.

title: The battle in the 380th year
summary: In the 380th year, the Lamanites come against the Nephites to battle. The Nephites stand against them boldly, but the Lamanites' great numbers overwhelm them.

explicit_facts.text: In the 380th year the Lamanites came against the Nephites to battle.
The Nephites stood against the Lamanites boldly, but were overwhelmed by their great numbers.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The two armies face each other, with the much larger Lamanite force pressing the Nephites back.
unspecified_visual_details: The battlefield, equipment, formation, and individual combatants.

narration.text: we did stand against them boldly

title: The Nephites flee
summary: The Nephites flee again. Those who flee faster than the Lamanites escape, while those who cannot outrun them are swept down and destroyed.

explicit_facts.text: The Nephites took flight again; those who were faster than the Lamanites escaped, and those who were not were swept down and destroyed.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The fleeing Nephites separate into those escaping and those overtaken.
unspecified_visual_details: The terrain, number of people, and the precise manner of destruction.

narration.text: we did again take to flight

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict wounds, blood, or severed body parts.

title: Mormon chooses an abridgment
summary: Mormon explains that he does not wish to describe the awful scene of blood and carnage he saw, but writes an abridgment because the things must be made known and hidden things revealed. He has received a commandment and seeks to spare readers excessive sorrow over the people's wickedness.

explicit_facts.text: Mormon did not wish to cast before readers the awful scene of blood and carnage he had seen.
Mormon says these things must be made known and hidden things revealed, so he writes a small abridgment under a commandment and to avoid causing too great sorrow.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mormon is shown writing, as the verse says he writes an abridgment.
unspecified_visual_details: The writing materials and setting; the scene Mormon saw is not depicted.

narration.text: I write a small abridgment
because of the wickedness of this people

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The blood and carnage are reported as what Mormon saw; do not stage them as a present event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show the carnage or add an audience for Mormon's writing.

title: Mormon addresses future readers
summary: Mormon addresses the people's seed and Gentiles who care for the house of Israel. He says they will sorrow over Israel's calamity and the people's destruction, and over their failure to repent and be clasped in Jesus's arms.

explicit_facts.text: Mormon says he speaks to the people's seed and to Gentiles who care for the house of Israel and recognize the source of their blessings.
Mormon says they will sorrow over Israel's calamity and the people's destruction and failure to repent.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mormon can be shown delivering this address as narration, without depicting the future readers.
unspecified_visual_details: The identities and appearance of the future readers; Jesus's appearance.

narration.text: this I speak unto their seed
they will sorrow for the destruction of this people

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The image of being clasped in Jesus's arms is expressed as a teaching, not a described visible event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict future readers or Jesus as physically present.

title: The record is reserved
summary: Mormon says the record is written for the remnant of Jacob's house and is to be hidden up unto the Lord until it comes forth in the Lord's due time, according to his commandment and wisdom.

explicit_facts.text: The writings are for the remnant of the house of Jacob and are to be hidden up unto the Lord until they come forth in his due time.
Mormon says this is the commandment he received and that the writings will come forth when the Lord sees fit, in his wisdom.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mormon may be shown with the written record as he speaks of it.
unspecified_visual_details: The record's physical form and the manner of its concealment or future emergence.

narration.text: they are to be hid up unto the Lord
in his own due time

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The future emergence is described in words, not shown as a present event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a supernatural appearance or an unmentioned act of hiding.

title: The record's purpose
summary: Mormon says the record will go to unbelieving Jews to persuade them that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of the living God, and that the Father may fulfill his eternal purpose in restoring the Jews, or all Israel, to their land and fulfilling his covenant.

explicit_facts.text: The record will go to unbelieving Jews to persuade them that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of the living God.
The Father is to bring about his purpose through his Beloved in restoring the Jews, or all Israel, to their land and fulfilling his covenant.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mormon may be shown narrating the record's purpose.
unspecified_visual_details: The Jews who will receive the record, the land's appearance, and Jesus's appearance.

narration.text: that Jesus is the Christ
the Son of the living God

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Restoration and covenant fulfillment are teachings and future events, not a present visual scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show a future restoration or invent the appearance of Jesus.

title: A warning about the people's future
summary: Mormon says the people's seed may more fully believe the gospel that will go forth from the Gentiles. He says this people will be scattered because of unbelief and idolatry, and that the Spirit has ceased striving with their fathers; they are without Christ and God and driven about as chaff.

explicit_facts.text: Mormon says the seed may more fully believe the gospel that will go forth from the Gentiles.
Mormon says the people will be scattered because of unbelief and idolatry, and describes them as without Christ and God and driven about as chaff.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mormon can be shown narrating; the scattering and chaff comparison need not be literalized.
unspecified_visual_details: The future people, the physical form of the scattering, and the appearance of the Spirit.

narration.text: this people shall be scattered
they are without Christ and God in the world

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Chaff driven by wind is a figure of speech, not a literal supernatural scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a visible Spirit or Christ in this moment.

title: From shepherded to adrift
summary: Mormon contrasts the people of the past, who had Christ as shepherd and were led by God the Father, with their present state, led about by Satan like wind-driven chaff or a vessel without sail, anchor, or steering.

explicit_facts.text: The people were once a delightsome people, with Christ as their shepherd and led by God the Father.
Mormon says they are now led about by Satan, like chaff before the wind or a vessel tossed on waves without sail, anchor, or steering.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Keep the past-versus-present comparison as narration rather than depicting divine or satanic figures.
unspecified_visual_details: The people's appearance and any literal vessel or shepherd.

narration.text: they had Christ for their shepherd
without sail or anchor

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The shepherd, chaff, and vessel images are figures of speech in this passage.
prohibited_inventions: Do not portray Christ, God, or Satan as visible figures.

title: Blessings and covenant remembrance
summary: Mormon says the Lord has reserved the people's potential blessings in the land for the Gentiles who will possess it. He says the people will be driven and scattered by the Gentiles, after which the Lord will remember the covenant to Abraham and Israel and the prayers of the righteous for them.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord reserved the people's blessings in the land for the Gentiles who will possess it.
After the people are driven and scattered by the Gentiles, the Lord will remember his covenant to Abraham and the house of Israel.
The Lord will remember the prayers of the righteous offered for them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mormon may be shown narrating these future and doctrinal statements.
unspecified_visual_details: The Gentiles, the land, Abraham, the righteous who prayed, and the manner of scattering.

narration.text: the Lord hath reserved their blessings
the Lord will remember the prayers of the righteous

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These are statements about future events and divine remembrance, not a present visual event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show a divine appearance or invent the future scattering as happening now.

title: Mormon warns the Gentiles
summary: Mormon asks how the Gentiles can stand before God's power without repenting and turning from evil. He calls them to repent and humble themselves, warning that a remnant of Jacob's seed may go among them as a lion and tear them in pieces, with none to deliver.

explicit_facts.text: Mormon asks the Gentiles how they can stand before God's power unless they repent and turn from evil.
Mormon says the Gentiles are in God's hands, that God has all power, and that at his command the earth shall be rolled together as a scroll.
Mormon commands the Gentiles to repent and humble themselves, warning that a remnant of Jacob's seed may go among them as a lion and tear them in pieces.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mormon is the visible narrator; the warning may be presented as off-screen speech without illustrating its figures literally.
unspecified_visual_details: The Gentiles being addressed, God's appearance, and the appearance of the remnant.

narration.text: repent ye, and humble yourselves before him
there is none to deliver

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The earth rolled as a scroll and the remnant as a lion are figurative warnings, not narrated visible events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict God, a world-ending event, or a literal lion attack.
